text: Huram king of Tyre sent messengers to David, along with cedar logs, masons, and carpenters to build him a palace.

versions.text: Hiram king of Tyre sent messengers to David, along with cedar logs, masons, and carpenters to build him a palace.
versions.explanation: The Hebrew reading tradition here, and the form used consistently elsewhere in Chronicles, is Huram; a footnote noting "also spelled Hiram" would help readers connect him with the parallel account.

text: So David knew that the LORD had established him as king over Israel, for his kingdom was highly exalted for the sake of his people Israel.
In Jerusalem David took more wives, and he fathered more sons and daughters.
These are the names of the children born to him in Jerusalem: Shammua, Shobab, Nathan, Solomon,
When the Philistines heard that David had been anointed king over all Israel, they all marched up to search him out. David heard of it and went out to face them.
The Philistines came and raided the Valley of Rephaim.
So David inquired of God, "Shall I attack the Philistines? Will you hand them over to me?" The LORD answered him, "Attack. I will hand them over to you."

So they went up to Baal-perazim, and there David struck them down. David said, "God has broken through my enemies by my hand like a bursting flood." That is why they named the place Baal-perazim, which means "the lord of breakthroughs."

versions.text: So they went up to Baal-perazim, and there David struck them down. David said, "God has broken through my enemies by my hand like a bursting flood." That is why they named the place Baal-perazim.
versions.explanation: The wordplay between David's words ("broken through") and the place name is invisible to English hearers. A brief in-text gloss (or a footnote reading "Baal-perazim means 'lord of breakthroughs'") preserves the sense of the naming formula.

text: The Philistines had abandoned their gods there, and at David's command they were burned in the fire.
Once again the Philistines raided the valley.
David inquired of God again, and God told him, "Do not go up after them. Circle around them and come at them in front of the balsam trees.
As soon as you hear the sound of marching in the tops of the balsam trees, go out to battle, for God has gone out ahead of you to strike down the Philistine army."
David did as God commanded him, and they struck down the Philistine army from Gibeon all the way to Gezer.
So David's fame spread through every land, and the LORD put the dread of David on all the nations.

versions.text: So David's fame spread through every land, and the LORD made all the nations fear him.
versions.explanation: In the current wording, "him" is ambiguous: the nearest antecedent is "the LORD," but the Hebrew pronoun in "his dread" (פַּחְדּוֹ) refers to David. Naming David removes the ambiguity for a listening audience.
